The story unfolds entirely in real-time through a dialogue-driven scene, aligning the "story time" almost one-to-one with the "real world time" it takes to read it. This lack of narrative compression or stretching within the action itself is highly appropriate and effective because it forces the reader to experience the awkward, hesitant rhythm of the characters' reunion firsthand. At the same time, the months or years the characters have spent apart are subtly "compressed" into brief, understated lines of subtext (e.g., "Schon im Februar," "Du bist dünner geworden," "Die blaue gibt es noch"). This creates a well-balanced pacing where the weight of a long absence is felt heavily within a single, quiet moment.
